As somebody mentioned earlier in the comments section: If you have anything that can fall outside the basic care, don't waste your time coming to this surgery, as you will be told that you will be okay if you change your diet, or just "let things go". ABSOLUTE JOKE!
A couple of things for doctors to consider:
1. BE HONEST. Why not telling the patient straight away, that you cannot offer a certain treatment? Why waste everyone's time? Just be honest and advice the patient that this service falls outside the basic NHS treatment allowance.. Advice such as: Let things go, and change your diet DO NOT WORK.
2. LEARN ABOUT MENTAL HEALTH. If you think that mental health issues are just imaginations of the person and do not affect their physical and mental wellbeing, which can be very painful and produce symptoms VERY similar to real diseases, then expand your knowledge and at least try to be understanding about the power of the mind.

On a positive note: They are quite good in helping if you have a minor, not serious condition. They have a physiotherapist on site, which is good as well. Plus you can get an appointment fairly quickly, which is also very good.

Advice for prospective patients: if you have a complicated/difficult to treat condition and are in possession of a bit of money, go private, don't waste your time.
